chunks: Ali (ibn al-Hakam) from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding

two witnesses testified against a woman that her husband had divorced her, so she married another man, then her first husband came and denied the divorce. He said: 'They are flogged (with the limit punishment) and are held liable for the dowry to the husband, then she observes her waiting period, then she returns to her first husband.'

key_terms.يُضْرَبَانِ اَلْحَدَّ: they are flogged (with the limit punishment)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal consequence for a woman and witnesses if a divorce is disputed after she has remarried?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the procedure for *Khul'* or contested divorce where the husband denies the initial testimony of two witnesses; the witnesses are flogged and guarantee the dowry (*sadaq*), ensuring the woman's financial security during her interim marriage. After observing the waiting period (*iddah*), she returns to her first husband, illustrating the Shia juristic emphasis on evidentiary standards and the protection of marital rights in cases of disputed divorce.
